metadata.case_name: LAM SIU PING v. THE SECRETARY FOR JUSTICE FOR AND ON BEHALF OF LEISURE AND CULTURAL SERVICES DEPARTMENT

plaintiff.occupation_before: Technician (gardening team), Leisure and Cultural Services Department (joined LCSD 31 October 1979; promoted Technician (gardening team) in 1989; assigned to Recreation Ground in 1996)
plaintiff.occupation_after: Technician (gardening team) at Leisure and Cultural Services Department (resumed pre-accident employment on 15 April 2007)

injuries.description: sprained his right shoulder and wrist
source: As a result, he sprained his right shoulder and wrist.

injuries.description: right wrist condition compatible with de Quervain’s disease
source: His right wrist condition was compatible with de Quervain’s disease.
injuries.icd_description: Other specified injury of extensor muscle, fascia or tendon of thumb at wrist or hand level

injuries.description: tear and tendonitis of right rotator cuff suspected; operative diagnosis '[shoulder] impingement syndrome (Rt)'; MRI suggestive of small tear of the supraspinatus
source: Tear and tendonitis of right rotator cuff were suspected due to the significant right shoulder pain.
the operative diagnosis was "[shoulder] impingement syndrome (Rt)".
At the follow up on 18 September 2006, the Plaintiff was advised MRI right shoulder was suggestive of a small tear of the supraspinatus.
injuries.icd_description: Strain or sprain of muscle or tendon of the rotator cuff of shoulder

source: the MRI done on 10 August 2009 revealed (a) osteoarthritis of acromioclavicular joint, (b) articular partial tear at supraspinatus tendon, and (c) interstitial partial tear at infraspinatus tendon.
injuries.icd_description: Injuries to the shoulder or upper arm

injuries.description: 1 x 0.6cm incomplete rotator cuff tear mainly on bursal side (repair done)
source: intra-operative finding was "1 x 0.6cm incomplete rotator cuff tear mainly on bursal side repair done".
injuries.icd_description: Other specified injury of muscle or tendon of the rotator cuff of shoulder

injuries.description: injury to his right middle finger (sprained right middle finger); day surgery for his right middle finger injury
source: it suddenly rebounded forward with great force and caused injury to his right middle finger (ie the 2nd Accident).
Day surgery for his right middle finger injury took place on 22 July 2009.
injuries.icd_description: Strain or sprain of finger, unspecified

source: The Plaintiff attended UCH’s AED on 5 June 2007 for right tennis elbow.
At the follow up on 11 June 2007, he was given a tennis elbow splint.
injuries.icd_description: Other specified injury of extensor muscle, fascia or tendon of other finger at forearm level

injuries.description: impression "? Chronic regional pain syndrome" (right upper limb)
source: The impression was "? Chronic regional pain syndrome for bone scan and pain team assessment to call back if ulcer showed growth".

manifestations.description: right shoulder pain causing numbness of right upper limb
aggravated right shoulder pain during humid and rainy weather
weakness of the right upper limb including inability to carry heavy object
reduced range of movement of right upper limb
right upper limb swelling, numbness, stiffness and resting pain
inability to make a full fist
diffuse tenderness and stiffness of wrist/fingers

treatments_received: Arthroscopy of right shoulder and arthroscopic acrominoplasty (operation performed 1 November 2005)
Further arthroscopy of shoulder, arthroscopic acrominoplasty and rotator cuff repair (operation performed 5 February 2010)
Day surgery for right middle finger injury (22 July 2009)
Physiotherapy (31 sessions from 3 November 2005 to 2 March 2006)
Physiotherapy (37 sessions from 6 February to 23 August 2010)

losses.description: HK$600,000.00 for pain, suffering and loss of amenities due to incapacity (including persistent residual pain and reduced mobility) as a result of the 1st and 2nd Accidents
HK$120,000 for reduction/limitation of chance for promotion to a higher rank and disadvantage in the labour market should he lose his job as a result of the 1st and 2nd Accidents
